ruling.recommended_action: Refer to RydeHELP human review: obtain the missing cancellation-party record (cancelled_by) for booking X-0012 and determine whether NS-1 or NS-4 governs the $6.61 fee; hold the fee pending that check.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service [F8], so no RD-2 money calculation arises; this is a cancellation-fee dispute and NS-0 is the only gateway, branching on cancelled_by — rider cancels goes to NS-4, a driver declaring a no-show goes to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The trace marks NS-0 as failed: the timeline records Cancelled by None at 17:32:45, 8 min 45 s after acceptance [F4], so no system record names the party that ended the booking. The rider's complaint attributes the disappearance to the platform, and the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is a statement, not a system record, and cannot supply the missing actor [F4][F11][NS-0].

Because the branch cannot be chosen, the outcome flips between two clauses on the same facts. Under NS-4 (rider cancelled), cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching makes the $6.61 fee payable, no_action [F4][NS-4]. Under NS-1 (driver cancelled declaring a no-show), all three elements are needed: an I'm Here tap (i), GPS at the pickup at that moment (ii), and continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes after the tap (iii). Elements (i) and (ii) are met — tap at 17:28:05, 42 m from pickup, within the 200 m radius, closest approach 4 m at 17:27:40 [F6][F1][NS-1]. Element (iii) is decided against the driver: the post-tap wait is 4 min 40 s [F6], short of the required more than 3 minutes (at least 3:01) counted from the tap, and the 5 min 40 s cumulative presence [F2] and the 5 min 0 s stationary period [F3] both begin before the 17:28:05 tap and are expressly excluded by NS-1(iii) [F3][F6][NS-1]. No case record carries a no_show_threshold_min, so the NS-1 default governs [F4][F6][NS-1]; on that reading NS-2 would require a full refund of $6.61 [F7][NS-2].

The two branches point to opposite results, so no amount can be computed and this is insufficient evidence, not mere uncertainty: the trace states the deciding field is missing and the only permitted outcome is escalation. I therefore rule escalate and leave amount null; the reviewer should pull the cancellation record (who pressed cancel, and whether a driver-side no-show declaration exists) and then apply NS-1 or NS-4 [F4][NS-0][NS-1][NS-4].

Safety screen: I read the single chat message — a neutral arrival notice, At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis, 17:28 [F9] — the complete timestamped chat record [F10], the driver's post-trip statement [F11], the rider's complaint, and the traffic and weather facts [F12][F13][F14]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

No flag_account: RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver (a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach), and no merits finding is made here; the profile fields are not used to decide anything [F16][F15][RD-6].
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: cancelled_by is not on record — the timeline shows Cancelled by None at 17:32:45 (F4). Without it NS-0 cannot route to NS-1 (driver declares a rider no-show; the fee would need a post-tap wait of at least 3:01, and F6 gives only 4 min 40 s measured from the tap) versus NS-4 (rider cancels after 3 minutes; the fee stands). No no_show_threshold_min is recorded either, so the NS-1 default applies. The record that would settle which clause governs is missing.

rejected_claims.reason: The refund_full conclusion rests on NS-1(iii) failing, but NS-1 only applies if the driver cancelled declaring a no-show; the record does not establish that (F4, cancelled_by = None), so NS-4 may equally govern and the fee may be payable [F4][NS-0][NS-4].

Its arithmetic is right (post-tap wait 4 min 40 s, F6, below the at-least-3:01 NS-1(iii) requirement, with F3 pre-tap time excluded), but it presumes the NS-1 branch applies; with the cancelling party unrecorded the branch cannot be fixed [F4][F6][NS-0][NS-1].

The rider's profile (0 disputes, 0 upheld, F15) cannot decide the fee, and profile facts never stand alone; her account of being on her way down is uncorroborated against the GPS arrival and waiting facts [F15][F2][F3][F5][NS-1].

No flag_account: RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver (a refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach), which this escalation does not find; the driver's single prior upheld no-show dispute (F16) cannot drive account action on profile alone [F16][RD-6].

Accepted on the safety screen — the single neutral arrival message, the complete timestamped chat and the driver's statement contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving material [F9][F10][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The 5 min 40 s arrival-to-cancellation interval (F5, F2) does not itself establish a rider no-show; NS-1 counts only continuous waiting after the I'm Here tap, and the timeline never records a driver cancellation declaring a no-show [F4][F2][F5][NS-1].

The 5 min 0 s stationary period (F3) begins 20 s before the 17:28:05 tap and the 5 min 40 s cumulative figure (F2) is pre-tap; NS-1(iii) excludes time before the tap, leaving only 4 min 40 s (F6), below the required at-least-3:01 [F3][F2][F6][NS-1].
The rider's complaint wording is not evidence of a fulfilled no-show; her account carries no corroborating record and cannot convert the post-tap wait into one satisfying NS-1(iii) [F3][F6][NS-1].
The driver's 90-day record (1 upheld no-show dispute, F16) is profile material and cannot decide the fee, and it does not support a flag_account absent an established case against him [F16][RD-6].
